items.title: Muggsy Spanier Interview, 1961-02-02
items.q: Well, George was with Ted Lewis about 16 years and I was with him about seven.

ctx.x: How long did you stay with Ted Lewis and how long was George with you at that time?
Well, George was with Ted Lewis about 16 years and I was with him about seven.
Was George there all the time you were there? Yes. Because all the records that you were on, George would be on then, too?

items.title: Georg Brunis Interview, 1958-06-03
items.q: And then Muggsy and I used to do a lot with Ted Lewis, and then we'd take the hats with that.

ctx.x: While we were talking about those different effects, did you ever use old things like derbies or the plunger?

Oh, yeah, yeah. I used a plunger on a record. I think it was Muggsy's Lonesome Road. People wrote in the crystal. What is that instrument on there? They didn't know it was a trombone. It was on Lonesome Road. And then Muggsy and I used to do a lot with Ted Lewis, and then we'd take the hats with that. Well, a lot of big bands are doing that now.
Tell me about back in New Orleans when you were a kid. Did they use anything? Some people said they used sugar cans or buckets and things over. What did you use?

items.title: George "Pops" Foster and Mugsy Spanier Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: Elmer Schovel was in the band, George Brunus.

ctx.x: I got some records. I bought some Jeanette records with Joe Alvarez. Oh yeah. So I was going on the south side, and I wanted to find out where Joe was working. At that time, he was working at the Dreamland. Yeah. 35th Estate. Yeah. One of them. He used to have Wednesday matinees. Oh yeah? So. I guess they didn't have any relish. They'd go down there every Wednesday afternoon. Mm-hmm. Sit on the bed. They'd let us sit. They'd sit up in the balcony and drink Coca-Cola. Oh, just move around. And then, I think after…
